problem: The symbol I<sub>earth</sub> is defined as 'enclosure or earth leakage' with a single 5 mA limit. These are two different measurements with very different limits. Earth leakage (current in the protective earth conductor) is ≤ 5 mA in normal condition, but enclosure leakage (case to earth through a person) is ≤ 100 µA in normal condition and ≤ 500 µA in single fault. A student who learns 5 mA as the enclosure limit will pass an unsafe device.
fix: Split the two: I<sub>earth</sub> (protective-earth-conductor leakage) ≤ 5 mA in normal condition; I<sub>enclosure</sub> (case to earth) ≤ 100 µA in normal condition and ≤ 500 µA in single fault; I<sub>patient</sub> ≤ 100 µA for B or BF and ≤ 10 µA for CF in normal condition.

problem: The trap repeats the same conflation: '5 mA is an earth or enclosure limit'. Enclosure leakage is a 100 µA limit, not 5 mA.
fix: '100 µA is the patient limit for B or BF; 5 mA is the earth-conductor leakage limit; the enclosure (case) leakage limit is 100 µA. Do not use the wrong number.'

problem: The answer gives the wrong fault. In the single-fault test the tester deliberately opens the protective earth, so a rise in leakage then is the device's own single-fault leakage (insulation, EMI-filter capacitors, mains-to-patient capacitance) exceeding the single-fault limit. A broken earth wire is a different fault that the earth-continuity test would already have caught.
fix: Answer: the device leaks too much when its earth reference is removed, so its insulation or its mains filter capacitance is excessive. Remove it from service, have it serviced (insulation, filter, mains-to-patient isolation checked), then repeat insulation resistance and single-fault leakage tests before use.

problem: The caption says to measure '... insulation resistance and leakage, and only then run the device'. Leakage current cannot be measured with the device off; the body of the chapter correctly says 'run the device and measure enclosure and patient leakage'. The two contradict each other and a student will think leakage is measured unpowered.
fix: Caption: 'inspect and unplug first, then measure earth continuity and insulation resistance unpowered; then power the device and measure leakage in normal and single-fault condition, and finish with the functional test.'

problem: Q1 asks for 'the four safety tests', but the chapter's own procedure has six steps (visual, earth continuity, insulation resistance, leakage, single-fault leakage, functional test), and the answer silently adds the functional test to the four.
fix: Ask: 'List the six steps of the safety check in order', answer: visual inspection, earth continuity, insulation resistance, leakage current in normal condition, leakage current in single-fault condition, functional test.

problem: 'breaks the earth path from the mains neutral to the device' is muddled. The transformer does not break the earth wire; it removes the earth reference of the secondary, so touching one live conductor does not complete a circuit through earth.
fix: 'An isolation transformer separates the device supply from the earthed mains, so the secondary has no reference to earth. A single contact with one live conductor then cannot drive current through the body to earth.'
